purpose: Small diversified comparison batch for confronting representation-selection hypotheses with real assets or concrete concepts before any automatic scoring is generalized to the 5504-sound exact lexical bank.

cases.representationPlan: Isolated bird nest made of twigs, with no bird, tree or egg dominating the scene.
cases.whyThisRoute: The lexical item is concrete, category-specific and visually compact; the existing research asset already isolates the intended object strongly enough to inspect selection assumptions before redrawing anything.
cases.nextDecision: Run a small naming observation on the existing asset before any redraw; compare responses such as nid, nid d'oiseau, panier or bol if they arise.

cases.representationPlan: Profile bust with the neck exposed; compare an uncued version against a version with a small visual pointer.
cases.whyThisRoute: The word is concrete but denotes a body part whose neighboring labels compete strongly, making it useful for testing whether specificity and cue need predict naming difficulty better than concreteness alone.
cases.nextDecision: Prototype only the minimal contrasted pair needed to test whether a pointer improves naming without becoming a hidden textual rule.

cases.representationPlan: Open school compass with its pencil leg visible, isolated from ruler, pencil case and geometry scene.
cases.whyThisRoute: A single recognizable two-syllable object can be preferable to two shorter ambiguous pieces; this case calibrates the value of long exact windows independently of piece count.
cases.nextDecision: Make one restrained prototype and compare its naming performance against the alternative shorter decomposition rather than rewarding shorter pieces by default.

cases.representationPlan: Visible capital letter A, explicitly interpreted by the general-rebus convention as the French letter name /a/.
cases.whyThisRoute: The exact lexical entry does not yield a naturally nameable object, while the letter-name convention is explicit, visible and semantically honest for playful rebus mode.
cases.nextDecision: Keep A as an explicit convention candidate; test comprehension of the convention separately from pictogram naming.

cases.representationPlan: A simple glass or splash of milk intended to evoke lait, only if the approximation remains visibly marked as playful/general-mode evidence.
cases.whyThisRoute: The object is easy to depict, but its pronunciation differs from /le/; it is therefore useful precisely as a calibration case for keeping visual promise separate from phonetic strictness.
cases.nextDecision: Retain only as a labeled playful fallback after exact and explicit-convention routes; never let visual obviousness upgrade it to strict.

cases.representationPlan: Thick muddy puddle with splashes, with no shoe, wheel or landscape dominating.
cases.whyThisRoute: The referent is concrete and graphic but belongs to a material/category cluster where terre, flaque and saleté may compete, offering a contrast with the more object-specific nid case.
cases.nextDecision: Use as a contrast case against nid: test whether lower object specificity predicts more category-label variation before encoding that property into the global map.

generalizationGate: Only promote a predictive property into the 5504-sound landscape after several cases and, where naming is at issue, real human observations show a repeatable relationship.
